title: Review, Verification & Competency Decisions
summary: Learn why evidence review, verification, and competency decisions are separate steps and why learners cannot simply mark their own skills as institutionally verified.
objectives: Explain why review is different from self-assessment.
Distinguish evidence status from a competency decision.
Recognize that authorized review may confirm, reject, or request stronger evidence.

vocab.def: An examination of evidence against defined expectations or requirements.
An authorized process that confirms a fact or evidence status according to the applicable system or rules.
A separately defined and assessable capability.
An authorized determination about whether available evidence supports a defined competency.

sections.heading: Self-reflection is valuable, but it is not institutional verification
sections.body: Learners should evaluate their own work and identify strengths and gaps. That reflection does not automatically become an institutional competency decision.

sections.heading: Evidence and competency are related but different
sections.body: Evidence provides information about work or performance. A competency decision interprets appropriate evidence against a defined capability.

sections.heading: Review can produce more than one outcome
sections.body: A reviewer may determine that evidence is sufficient, insufficient, incomplete, unrelated, or in need of clarification depending on the applicable process.

sections.heading: Completion does not automatically mean competency
sections.body: Finishing a lesson or course can establish completion when the completion authority says so. It does not automatically establish a separately governed competency.

practice.prompt: A learner finishes every lesson in a course. Does that alone automatically create a verified competency?
practice.answer: No. Completion and competency verification are separate authorities.

practice.prompt: A learner believes their project proves a skill. What is the appropriate next step when formal verification is required?
practice.answer: Submit or route the eligible evidence through the applicable authorized review process.

quiz.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Evidence can support a competency decision, but the learner does not create the institutional verification decision
Lesson completion automatically verifies every related competency
A reflection can mark institutional evidence verified
quiz.answer: Evidence can support a competency decision, but the learner does not create the institutional verification decision

lab.objective: Review simulated cases and identify whether each represents self-reflection, evidence submission, evidence review, completion, or a competency decision.

reflectionPrompt: Why is it useful for a competency decision to remain separate from your own opinion about your work?
